props.text: New England already has regional skiing, so Aspen from Boston tends to be the once-a-season bigger trip, not a casual weekend. Flying out of BOS, a trip to Oaxaca can start around $1,266 for flight, hotel, and activities together — not just the flight, pulled from our own cost data, not guesses.

features.title: Cancún — nonstop, ~4h20m
features.text: JetBlue and Delta both fly it direct.

features.title: Oaxaca — no nonstop
features.text: The fastest routing, via Dallas on American, runs about 8h19m total.

features.title: Aspen — no nonstop at all
features.text: Mostly routes via Denver, also Chicago, Dallas, or Atlanta; the shortest connection still runs about 7h13m.

props.text: Cancún's nonstop and Boston's large college-age travel population make it the default easy pick. Aspen, despite requiring the longest connection of the three, still draws real demand from Boston — it reads as the bigger, once-a-season ski trip precisely because New Englanders already have regional mountains for anything more casual. Oaxaca, at 8+ hours connecting, is best treated as a deliberate 5-day-plus cultural trip, not a long weekend.

items.question: Are these real-time prices?
items.answer: They're estimates based on our own curated cost data for this route and season, not a live quote — the real price on the partner site may be a bit higher or lower depending on exact dates.

items.question: Is Oaxaca doable as a long weekend from Boston?
items.answer: It's tight — the fastest connection runs about 8h19m each way, so realistically you'll want 5 or more days to make the travel time worth it.

items.question: Is Aspen worth the trip from Boston?
items.answer: There's no nonstop — connections run 7h13m or more each way — so it's a bigger commitment than a quick ski weekend, which is why it tends to be the once-a-season trip rather than a regular one.
